items.text: The team has decided to develop a remote control that is original, trendy, appealing to a wide market, user-friendly, and accessible to people of all ages including grannies and even pets.
The functional design process will be broken into three phases: functional design (what needs the product fulfills), conceptual design (how it will work), and detailed design (how it will be built).
Each team member will draw their favorite animal on the whiteboard and describe its key characteristics.
Speaker S4 will leave space at the bottom of the whiteboard for their drawing, indicating they are short and will stand on a chair.
The team will discuss and document the selling price of the remote control, which is set at 25 euros.
Speaker S1 will record and store meeting notes in a shared folder for future reference.
The team will consider whether to undercut the price to remain competitive, but will assess if it might make the product appear cheap.
The team has identified three key characteristics of a dog: it is supportive, loyal, and has intuition (e.g., detecting a thief).
The team has identified that the animal chosen by Speaker S3 is a crocodile, which is described as scary and independent.
The team has identified that the animal chosen by Speaker S4 is an eagle, which is described as free-spirited, independent, and skilled at flying.
The team has determined that the selling price of 25 euros is equivalent to approximately 17 pounds.
What is the exact exchange rate between euros and pounds to determine the selling price in pounds?
Explore the integration of an LCD display and menu-based navigation in the remote control design, inspired by mobile phone interfaces.
Design a remote control with basic functions (on/off, volume, channel) and a section that opens to reveal advanced functions via intuitive menus.
Consider a flip-top remote control design that reveals a larger screen when flipped over, to improve usability and reduce bulk.
Include a large print mode or extra button for older users who may struggle with small text or symbols.
Ensure the remote control is user-friendly for older generations, avoiding complex layouts with tiny buttons or unfamiliar symbols.
Evaluate the feasibility and cost implications of incorporating LCD screens or mobile-style menus, especially given budget constraints.
Assess whether the remote control should adopt a minimalist, plastic-based design that is lightweight and easy to produce, rather than being fashion-focused.
The remote control should be designed to be accessible and usable by all age groups, including older users who may not be familiar with complex interfaces or digital menus.
The design should prioritize simplicity and intuitiveness over advanced features or fashion, focusing on core functions and clear visual cues.
The remote control should not require programming or complex setup, as this may be a barrier for older users or those unfamiliar with technology.
The product should be accessible internationally, targeting markets such as Australia and the United States, without requiring language-specific adaptations.
The remote control should avoid overwhelming users with too many buttons or symbols, instead using clear, recognizable icons and a hierarchical menu system.
